# Online Journal of Communication and Media Technologies

> A peer-reviewed, open-access academic journal publishing cutting-edge research in communication, media studies, and technology.

OJCMT is an international scholarly publication indexed in Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, covering topics ranging from social media and polarization to AI in journalism and emerging communication technologies. The journal is published by Bastas Publications and maintains rigorous peer-review standards with a focus on contemporary media and communication challenges.

## Key Topics

- peer-reviewed research
- open-access publishing
- communication and media studies
- social media and polarization
- artificial intelligence in journalism
- journal metrics and indexing
- videoconference fatigue
- publication ethics
- Scopus and JCR indexing
- CiteScore impact metrics
- generative AI policy
- platformized public sphere
- investigative journalism
- CC-BY Creative Commons licensing
- academic publishing standards

## Journal Overview

- [Homepage](https://www.ojcmt.net): Main entry point for the Online Journal of Communication and Media Technologies
- [Journal Description](https://www.ojcmt.net/home/journal-description): Publication details, ISSN 1986-3497, and comprehensive journal information
- [Aims and Scope](https://www.ojcmt.net/home/aims): Journal mission and research scope for communication and media studies
- [Publisher Information](https://www.ojcmt.net/home/publisher): Publisher details: Bastas Publications DOO, Podgorica, Montenegro

## Current Research

- [Current Issue](https://www.ojcmt.net/current-issue): Volume 16, Issue 2 with latest peer-reviewed research articles
- [Social Media Fragmentation and Polarization in the Platformized Public Sphere](https://www.ojcmt.net/article/social-media-fragmentation-and-polarization-in-the-platformized-public-sphere-making-the-case-for-18142): Research article examining social media polarization and WhatsApp's role in digital fragmentation
- [AI in the Newsroom: A Case Study of Investigative Journalists in Spain](https://www.ojcmt.net/article/ai-in-the-newsroom-a-case-study-of-investigative-journalists-in-spain-18148): Empirical case study on artificial intelligence integration in Spanish investigative journalism practices
- [Exploring Time-Lagged Effects and Gendered Differences of Videoconference Fatigue](https://www.ojcmt.net/article/exploring-time-lagged-effects-and-gendered-differences-of-videoconference-fatigue-on-work-family-18150): Empirical study investigating videoconference fatigue impacts and gender-based differences in remote work
